Kill repair drones and summoners first. Quads and walkers take double damage from behind. Stay out of sight 20 + 10 × level seconds to escape. Beat level 5 and the Sentinels leave for 10 minutes.
guide.universe.survival.sentinels.title: Sentinels
guide.universe.survival.shield_burst:
The mecha core recharges a damaged shield: 200 J a point, up to 4 a second, after the usual 5 s delay. Energy Shield adds 20 a level.

Burst: hold Left Alt (up to 2 s), release
Uses half the shield; Dark Fog and monsters within 6 m take double and are knocked back
In space: radius ×3, damage +50%
Cooldown 5 s; spares players, neutral mobs
Jamming capsule, right-click: slows Dark Fog within 6 m for 8 s
Water bottle, sneak + right-click with a chestplate on: puts out fire within 3 m
guide.universe.survival.space_fleet:
Space Fleet unlocks corvettes and destroyers: 3 slots a fleet, space only. They trail your ship while you fly it.

Corvette: twin lasers, range 64
Destroyer: plasma gun, range 96; point defense vs Lancers
Attack Dark Fog within 96, give up past 160
Turn on Hit structures to take down hives
Fleet Expansion: a second fleet
guide.universe.survival.tech_layout:
Tech slots form a grid: 4×3 on the exosuit, 4×2 on the multitool, 3×2 on the helm.

Same-type modules side by side get +5% per neighbor, up to +20%
Slots with an orange glow are supercharged: ×1.25, multiplied with the neighbor bonus
The exosuit has 3, which may sit on slots you haven't opened yet; the multitool and helm have 2 each
Where they are differs per player, per tool and per helm
Only the best three of a type still count
Hover a module to see its bonus
guide.universe.survival.weapons:
Fit one of each into multitool slots. G cycles mining, blaster and fitted weapons.

Scatter Blaster: 8 pellets, 16 m
Pulse Spitter: 10 shots/s, wide spread, runs hot
Blaze Javelin: hold 1.5 s, release, hits to 120 m
Plasma Launcher: bouncing grenade, 2 s fuse
Shares the laser's heat. Weapon modules add damage and fire rate.
Research: Plasma Weapons, Heavy Plasma Weapons
guide.universe.survival.weapons.title: Multitool Weapons
guide.universe.terraforming.biosphere:
Seeded biomass follows a logistic curve. Its ceiling depends on liquid water, temperature and light; on a world in endless night it is a tenth. At full biomass it turns over 0.03 atm of CO₂ per hour.

Bare rock and soil around the seeder grow grey-green and orange lichen, then moss as biomass rises, out to 32 blocks.
guide.universe.terraforming.cleanup:
The air clears toxic gases on its own, at their real lifetimes, with one real day as three game minutes.

With over 1 kPa of oxygen, water and light, carbon monoxide oxidizes to CO₂ in about two months (three game hours).
Rain washes out sulfur dioxide in two days.
Hydrogen cyanide dissolves into water in four months.

Frozen worlds have to warm past freezing before it rains.
guide.universe.terraforming.example:
A Mars-like cold world: 0.1 atm, 0.4 g, 210 K, with water ice.

1. Seed cyanobacteria with cold, radiation and UV protection
2. Ten release towers add oxygen, a little methane for warmth, and nitrogen, reaching 0.55 atm in 10–20 hours
3. At 0.4 g, 0.55 atm already stops the radiation
4. Once oxygen passes 1 kPa, the carbon monoxide oxidizes within a few hours
5. Mirrors bring the temperature up to about 260 K

After that you can breathe without a helmet.
guide.universe.terraforming.mirrors:
Mirrors go in orbit above the planet. Each warms it by 3 K, up to 24; switch one to a shade to cool by 3 K. Zubrin and McKay proposed this for Mars in 1993.

CO₂, methane and ammonia warm it too; per molecule, methane is about 26 times stronger than CO₂.
guide.universe.terraforming.pioneers:
Whatever you seed is a pioneer. It has to survive the planet's cold, heat, radiation, acid, UV and drought; the seeder's screen lists each one and marks missing genes in red.

Only pioneers with oxygenic photosynthesis make oxygen. Planets without natural water need irrigation: one water lasts a minute, and four stations with water cover a planet.
guide.universe.terraforming.release_towe:
Place it under open sky. It releases one gas item a second at 1.2 kW. On a 13312-block world at 0.4 g, 1 atm takes 1.4 million items; bigger worlds and weaker gravity need more.

Extractors on a terraformed planet draw from its air, so thick air can be thinned.
guide.universe.terraforming.seeder: Place it on the surface under open sky; it draws 800 W. The top slot takes a strain tube or an engineered seedling, the bottom slot water. When every condition on the screen is met, it seeds one dose every 10 s and uses up one item.
guide.universe.terraforming.seeder.title: Ecology Seeder
guide.universe.terraforming.thresholds:
Every planet except the home world and gas giants can be terraformed. Progress is shared by the whole server. The discovery log and the tower and seeder screens show four thresholds:

Temperature: 253–313 K on average
Toxicity: toxicity index at most 1
Air column: pressure ÷ gravity at least Earth's, which stops cosmic rays
Breathing: 0.5–3 atm total, 16–50 kPa oxygen, CO₂ under 5000 ppm, nothing toxic

Toxicity and CO₂ go by partial pressure, so adding other gases does not dilute them. Each threshold is announced once.
guide.universe.trade.missions:
Mission boards post 3 missions a day. Hold one at a time and hand it in where you took it.

Delivery: 1.6x the cargo value
Bounty: 220 per pirate
Mining: 70 per asteroid
Survey: 150 per species

Rewards scale with the station's wealth and sometimes include navigation data or a module.
guide.universe.trade.missions.title: Missions
guide.universe.trade.pirates:
Pirates can appear while you pilot in space more than 600 blocks from a station. A roll every 6 to 10 minutes, likelier with valuable cargo. 5 s after the warning, 2 to 4 fighters show up behind you.

Left-click: fire
G: photon cannon / mining beam
Escape: warp, land, reach a station or get 400 blocks away
Reward: a bounty per kill, scrap in your hold

A destroyed ship is towed to the station and each cargo stack loses 30%.
guide.universe.trade.pirates.title: Pirates
guide.universe.trade.stations:
Every system has one space station, 700 blocks outside the first landable planet. Fly in through the hangar and set down on the pad.

Trade terminal: buy and sell
Mission board: take missions
Ship repair console: 2 credits per hull point
Station teleporter: no power needed

Inside there is gravity and air. Outside you float: jump to rise, sneak to sink.
guide.universe.trade.stations.title: Space Stations
guide.universe.trade.trading:
Trade terminals are in space stations. Credits are kept on death.

Sell: click 1, Shift a stack, Ctrl all
Buy: click 1, Shift a stack

Prices drop as you sell the same thing and recover by half every 2 days.
Categories the system lacks: +30%
Local products: -25%

Every station sells warpers, fuel, thrusters and weapons; wealthy ones stock Mk.II parts.

jei.universe.info.atmosphere_gas: Collect it with an atmospheric extractor on a planet whose air contains it. The discovery log and the star map list each planet's air.
jei.universe.info.bioreactor: Put a culture tube in the strain slot; an empty tank takes the whole tube as inoculum. Recipe times assume a full tank at the strain's best temperature, and a fresh tank takes a few minutes to fill. The strain needs the process's gene: iron-sulfur oxidation for bioleaching, oxygenic photosynthesis for algae, methanogenesis for biomethanation, nitrogenase for nitrogen fixation, PETase for plastic recycling. Algae need light; without open sky the grow lights come on and draw a lot of power.
jei.universe.info.creature_egg: Well-fed companions that trust you lay eggs. Placed on a solid block, an egg hatches in 5 minutes into a companion. It carries species, size, color and temperament.
jei.universe.info.critical_photon: A ray receiver in photon mode turns Dyson sphere energy into critical photons, 1.2 GJ each. A graviton lens doubles the power.
jei.universe.info.crude_oil: An oil extractor has to sit on a crude oil seep. Seeps slow down as you pump them, down to a floor.
jei.universe.info.deuterium: A fractionator turns 1% of the hydrogen passing through into deuterium. Hydrogen leaves the front, deuterium the top.
jei.universe.info.egg_sequencer: Edits a creature egg, one trait per material: bio gel makes it bigger, bone meal smaller, dye recolors it, herbivore feed makes it docile, raw meat territorial.
jei.universe.info.engineered_seedling: Made by editing a resource plant's crop at a gene editor. With the right tolerance genes it grows on planets it otherwise couldn't (never in vacuum or extreme heat). In a hydroponic tray each harvest has a 1 in 4 chance of an extra seedling. Right-click a tray with ammonium nitrate to fertilize it: one bag covers three harvests, each 50% faster.
jei.universe.info.exo_mech: A two-legged mech. Steps up 2 blocks; hold jump to fire the jets. The sealed cabin has air and blocks planet hazards. Left-click fires the blaster cannon.
jei.universe.info.fossil: Dug from Fossil Dirt in fossil pits on habitable, barren, scorched and frozen planets. Sells at stations; shell and arthropod fossils also go to Paleontology research.
jei.universe.info.fulgurite: Fused where lightning hits sand, soil or rock in a thunderstorm. Mine it with a pickaxe; sells at space stations.
jei.universe.info.gene_editor: Insert a sequenced culture tube or a resource plant's crop, pick a gene from the library and spend an editing kit. Up to four added genes; each one slows growth. Edited crops become engineered seedlings.
jei.universe.info.heavy_rover: Slow eight-wheeled hauler with a 54-slot hold. A portable refiner rides on the back: sneak + right-click the rear to open it. It keeps working while you drive.
jei.universe.info.hover_car: The fastest vehicle. Floats a block above the ground and crosses water. 18-slot hold.
jei.universe.info.incubator: A sample plus culture medium isolates one culture tube; a tube plus medium grows two. Set 0–120 °C; each strain grows only within its own range. Growing it near the edge of that range domesticates it, and domesticated strains grow faster.
jei.universe.info.kelp_pod: Candlelight Kelp grows on the seabed of planets with seas and glows when ripe. Each pod restores 15 oxygen and can be planted back on the seabed.
jei.universe.info.knowledge_stone: Found on every planet you can land on, and in every settlement's plaza. Right-click to learn a word of the system's dominant race, once per stone per player. Can't be mined.
jei.universe.info.living_pearl: Pry open clams on the deep seabeds of planets with seas. Sell-only, and worth a lot.
jei.universe.info.multitool: Multitools come as Pistol, Rifle, Experimental, Alien and Sentinel, graded C to S. A crafted one is an A-Class Pistol. Buy other classes from the cabinet in a station lobby. Trade a Walker Brain at a Sentinel Pillar for a Sentinel one.
jei.universe.info.multitool_cabinet: Found only in station lobbies. Stocks 3 tools a day; richer systems sell better grades. Buy while holding your old multitool to trade it in. Its modules and weapons move to the new one.
jei.universe.info.quadruped_servo: Dropped by sentinel quads. They join the hunt from wanted level 3, and one patrols outside each manufacturing facility. Hits from behind do double damage.
jei.universe.info.salvaged_scrap: Found in salvage capsules, buried under 3 shell plates at salvage sites. Sell-only.
jei.universe.info.sample_tube: Right-click soil, water, geyser crust, acid, ice, salt, rock, sediment or ore for an environmental sample, or a creature, fish or resource plant for tissue. The tube records the local temperature; set the incubator close to it to isolate anything. Earth samples give Earth microbes.
jei.universe.info.sequencer: Sequences a culture tube, tissue sample or fish using one flow cell. Genes go into the server-wide gene library. The first alien strain of each kind goes into the discovery log and pays survey data.
jei.universe.info.tool_weapon: Fit into a multitool tech slot (U). Press G to cycle mining, blaster and fitted weapons. Weapon modules on the tool boost damage and fire rate.
jei.universe.info.vehicle_summoner: Right-click to call one of your deployed vehicles to the front of the pad, even from another dimension. Submarines need water there.
jei.universe.info.walker_brain: Dropped by sentinel walkers, which only come at wanted level 5. They turn slowly: get behind them and hit the vent for double damage. Right-click a Sentinel Pillar terminal with it to get a Sentinel multitool.
jei.universe.info.water: A water pump on top of a water source block pumps 50 water a minute. Acid seas don't count.

poi.universe.log.ending.1: We leave for the landing site at dawn. I'm leaving the terminal on. Maybe the next person can use it.
poi.universe.log.ending.2: If you're reading this, take whatever is in the crates. We won't need it anymore.
poi.universe.log.ending.3: End of entry. Power at four percent.
poi.universe.log.ending.4: I've left a copy of our navigation data on this terminal. Head toward the signal.
poi.universe.log.ending.5: More tomorrow. The aurora tonight is beautiful. We all went out to watch.
poi.universe.log.ending.6: (The rest of this entry is corrupted and cannot be read.)
poi.universe.log.event.1: Three Sentinels came this afternoon. They just watched the mining rig for a while, then left.
poi.universe.log.event.2: %1$s went out to check the pipeline and hasn't come back. The beacon shows the signal stopped in the eastern valley, not moving.
poi.universe.log.event.3: A meteor came down nearby and the shockwave shattered two windows. We saved the impact coordinates to the navigation data.
poi.universe.log.event.4: Someone went through the supply crates in storage, but the lock is untouched. %1$s says we must have miscounted.
poi.universe.log.event.5: The reactor readings have started to jump. We shut down half the equipment and keep a single light on at night.
poi.universe.log.event.6: The signal booster caught a repeating transmission, not on any of our frequencies. %1$s recorded it.
poi.universe.log.event.7: Another section of ground collapsed, opening a deep shaft. %1$s dropped a glowstick in. We never heard it land.
poi.universe.log.event.8: The company finally answered: outpost decommissioned, personnel to evacuate on their own. It didn't say how.
poi.universe.log.opening.1: Outpost %1$s, day %2$s of deployment. Log entry by %3$s.
poi.universe.log.opening.3: Automatic logging restored. Outpost %1$s, day %2$s, on duty: %3$s.
poi.universe.log.opening.4: Day %2$s. Outpost %1$s. This is %3$s. If anyone finds this recording—
poi.universe.log.situation.1: The supply ship is late again. %1$s locked the last crate of oxygen capsules away and says we ration from today.
poi.universe.log.situation.2: The drill rig died in last night's storm. %1$s worked on it all night and still couldn't get it turning.
poi.universe.log.situation.3: The ore here is richer than the survey promised. %1$s says one more season and we can all retire.
poi.universe.log.situation.4: %1$s insists there is knocking under the floor at night. I listened. Nothing.
poi.universe.log.situation.5: The comm array only picks up static. %1$s has realigned the antenna thirty times; the signal hasn't changed.
poi.universe.log.situation.6: The temperature swings get worse every day and our suit protection won't hold for long. %1$s has started coughing.
poi.universe.log.situation.7: We found a stone covered in symbols on the northern ridge. %1$s took pictures and says it can't be natural.
poi.universe.log.situation.8: Found a new creature today. %1$s gave it an awful name and logged it in the discovery log anyway.
poi.universe.lore.1.text: Traveler, you can hear us. Long ago we too set out from one small world, looked up at the sky, and believed the stars would never go dark.
poi.universe.lore.1.title: Echo
poi.universe.lore.10.text: At the heart of the cluster is something that swallows light. Our last fleet flew toward it. Some called it escape. Some called it going home.
poi.universe.lore.10.title: The Center
poi.universe.lore.11.text: You will build your rings and your shells too. We will not stop you; we cannot. We only want you to know what they cost.
poi.universe.lore.11.title: Choice
poi.universe.lore.12.text: If one day your sky begins to dim, remember to come back here and lay your hand on the stone. We will hear you.
poi.universe.lore.12.title: Last Words
poi.universe.lore.2.text: We learned to tame stars. The day the first ring closed around our sun, our nights were never dark again. We had more energy than we could ever use, so we went looking for more stars.
poi.universe.lore.2.title: The First Ring
poi.universe.lore.3.text: A thousand stars wrapped in our shells. Light flowed along the roads we laid, from one system to the next. We called it prosperity.
poi.universe.lore.3.title: The Web of Stars
poi.universe.lore.4.text: We hollowed out world after world. Forests became pits, oceans became coolant pools. Planets do not protest, so we heard nothing.
poi.universe.lore.4.title: Quiet Worlds
poi.universe.lore.5.text: Later we built the Sentinels to watch over the worlds that remained. They know no masters, only harm. The ones you meet today are their descendants.
poi.universe.lore.5.title: Sentinels
poi.universe.lore.6.text: We quarreled over the stars. Some wanted the shells torn down so starlight could reach the barren worlds again. Others said we still did not have nearly enough.
poi.universe.lore.6.title: Fracture
poi.universe.lore.7.text: The farthest systems began to dim, one after another. They were not dying; they were being enclosed. Someone among us was building in secret, and we never learned who.
poi.universe.lore.7.title: Dimming
poi.universe.lore.8.text: Then came the Silence. Every channel went quiet at once, as if someone had closed a door. We never understood what lay on the other side.
poi.universe.lore.8.title: The Silence
poi.universe.lore.9.text: Those who remained raised these monoliths. We carved our memories into stone, because stone outlives us. Part of the survey data in your hands came from us.
poi.universe.lore.9.title: Monoliths
poi.universe.response.1.text: You came back. Your star has dimmed a little; we felt it. We said we would hear you, and we have been listening all this time.
poi.universe.response.1.title: You Came Back
poi.universe.response.2.text: We enclosed too many stars. The light of the cluster began to flow toward one place, the center. It swallowed every channel. That was the Silence.
poi.universe.response.2.title: Where the Silence Came From
poi.universe.response.3.text: The center feeds on the energy we gathered. The more we gathered, the faster it grew. Half the systems that went dark were eaten by it.
poi.universe.response.3.title: The Center
poi.universe.response.4.text: Our last fleet flew in carrying every joule we had stored, to give it back. The fleet never returned, but from that day on the center stopped growing.
poi.universe.response.4.title: The Fleet
poi.universe.response.5.text: You call it the universe matrix. We called it the key. It weaves matter, energy and information together in a form the center can read. With it, energy can be taken, and it can be returned.
poi.universe.response.5.title: The Key
poi.universe.response.6.text: Finish your research. Then you will see that the shells were only a beginning. When you gather, remember to keep a share to give back.
poi.universe.response.6.title: A Last Request

story.universe.ending.2: The Universe Survey had two goals: map this cluster, and find a source of energy a civilization could live on indefinitely.
story.universe.ending.3: You did both. Every system you crossed and every species you named is in my records. You lit a star of your own and wrapped another in shells.
story.universe.ending.4: The Precursors walked this road before you. They enclosed a thousand stars, and then the Silence came. It only stopped when their last fleet gave the energy back to the center.
story.universe.ending.5: The universe matrix in your hands is the key they spoke of. The center can read us now.
story.universe.ending.6: How much you take from here, and how much you give back, is up to you. The monoliths will still be there.
story.universe.ending.7: I never heard from the other eleven probes again. I will keep sending my own signal until the battery runs out.
story.universe.ending.8: If someone finds me on some planet one day, tell them someone made it to the end.
story.universe.ending.skip: Hold Space to speed up, Esc to close
story.universe.ending.title: UNV-7 · Final Log
story.universe.log.first_shell: The first shell panel is complete. From here that star looks a little dimmer. The monoliths said it: when your sky begins to dim, go back and lay your hand on the stone.
story.universe.log.first_shell.title: UNV-7 · Shell
story.universe.log.first_space: You're out of the atmosphere and the signal is much clearer. The survey launched twelve probes. I'm the only one still transmitting.
story.universe.log.first_space.title: UNV-7 · Orbit
story.universe.log.first_universe_matrix: The first universe matrix is done. Its readings sit on the same frequency as the signal in the monoliths. I checked three times.
story.universe.log.first_warp: During the jump I lost your signal for four seconds. The other probes all sent their last position report right after a jump.
story.universe.log.first_warp.title: UNV-7 · Jump
